slides.0.title: Course Introduction
slides.0.content:
Arriving at Centre-Loire means the Loire River journey is approaching its source — the climate here has shifted to semi-continental, and the soils switch from Tuffeau tuffstone to the trio of Kimmeridgian marl, Silex flint, and chalky limestone from the Late Jurassic. Sancerre and Pouilly-Fumé face each other across the river, yet they represent the highest benchmark for Sauvignon Blanc on the world stage.

Course Learning Objectives

🪨 Three-Soil System

Master how Caillottes (chalk), Terres Blanches (Kimmeridgian), and Silex (flint) shape the diversity of Sauvignon Blanc

🔥 The Mystery of Flint Smokiness

Understand the chemical basis of pierre à fusil aromas and the naming origin of Pouilly-Fumé

⚖️ Sancerre vs Pouilly-Fumé Comparison

Build the ability to distinguish the two major AOCs: geography, soils, varietal diversity, and style expression

🌟 Producers and Wines

Get acquainted with key Centre-Loire producers: Henri Bourgeois, Edmond Vatan, Didier Dagueneau, and others
slides.1.title: Centre-Loire — Gems at the Loire River's Source
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Semi-Continental Climate
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Cold winters and hot summers with large temperature swings; grapes retain concentrated aromas, though spring frost risk exists
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Loire River Source
slides.1.highlights.1.content: The Loire winds between the Sancerre plateau and the Pouilly plain; river influence moderates the microclimate
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Two Main Varieties
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Sauvignon Blanc dominates for white; Pinot Noir makes rosé and red (only Sancerre is permitted to make red)
slides.1.content:
Centre-Loire is located south of Bourges in central France, over 700 km from the Loire's mouth. The climate, soils, and grape varieties here are completely different from the Muscadet and Anjou's Chenin Blanc world to the west — Sauvignon Blanc has found its spiritual origin here.

📐 Centre-Loire Key Facts

  • Main AOCs: Sancerre, Pouilly-Fumé, Pouilly-sur-Loire, Menetou-Salon, Quincy, Reuilly, Coteaux-du-Giennois, Châteaumeillant
  • Vineyard area: ~6,500 ha (approximately 12% of Loire Valley)
  • Main varieties: Sauvignon Blanc (white), Pinot Noir (red/rosé)
  • Climate: Semi-continental, average annual temperature 11–12°C, annual rainfall ~600 mm
  • Main threat: Spring frost (April late frost can destroy an entire year's production)
slides.1.quiz.question: Why is Centre-Loire's climate so different from the western Muscadet region?
slides.1.quiz.options.0: Centre-Loire is far from the ocean, shifting to a semi-continental climate with larger temperature swings and colder winters
slides.1.quiz.options.2: Centre-Loire is in a valley and has a milder climate
slides.1.quiz.options.3: Centre-Loire is influenced by the Mediterranean
slides.1.quiz.explanation: Centre-Loire is approximately 350 km from the Atlantic and has moved beyond oceanic climate influence. The semi-continental climate brings significant diurnal and seasonal temperature variation — the critical condition for Sauvignon Blanc to develop concentrated aromas and mineral tension — but also brings spring frost risk (e.g., 2016, 2017, 2021 vintages suffered multiple losses).
slides.4.title: Sancerre's Three-Soil System
slides.4.highlights.0.title: Caillottes (Chalky Limestone)
slides.4.highlights.0.content: ~40% of Sancerre; young and approachable, fresh citrus aromas
slides.4.highlights.1.title: Terres Blanches (Kimmeridgian Marl)
slides.4.highlights.1.content: ~40%; shares origin with Chablis, structured and deep minerality
slides.4.highlights.2.title: Silex (Flint)
slides.4.highlights.2.content: ~20%; rarest, producing the most age-worthy, smoky flint-driven style
slides.4.content:
What makes Sancerre complex and captivating is that three completely different soil types coexist within the same AOC. Each soil type gives Sauvignon Blanc a unique personality, making Sancerre not just "one flavor" but "a terroir spectrum."

🥌 Caillottes (Small Chalky Limestone)

Geology: White small limestone blocks formed in the Middle Jurassic

Distribution: Bué, Crézancy, Sury-en-Vaux villages

Characteristics: Excellent drainage, heats quickly, low water retention

Style: Fresh citrus, green apple, white flowers; approachable young (2–4 years)

Key producers: Pascal Jolivet, Domaine Vacheron (some cuvées)

🧱 Terres Blanches (Kimmeridgian Marl)

Geology: Late Jurassic, rich in marine fossils (Exogyra virgula oyster fossils)

Distribution: Chavignol, Verdigny (western Sancerre)

Characteristics: Good water retention, mineral-rich, same soil type as Chablis

Style: Firm structure, chalky mineral, damp herbal, 5–10 year aging potential

Key producers: François Cotat, Edmond Vatan, Henri Bourgeois

🔥 Silex (Flint)

Geology: Late Cretaceous, black hard flint fragments

Distribution: Ménétréol-sous-Sancerre, Saint-Satur (eastern Sancerre, near Loire River)

Characteristics: Absorbs heat quickly, slowly releases it at night, good heat retention

Style: Smoky pierre à fusil, gunpowder, high-acid mineral tension; 10+ year aging

Key producers: Domaine Vacheron Belle Dame, Lucien Crochet Cuvée Prestige
slides.4.quiz.question: Of Sancerre's three soil types, which shares the same origin as Chablis?
slides.4.quiz.explanation: Terres Blanches is the French name for Kimmeridgian marl, formed in Late Jurassic shallow marine environments, rich in Exogyra virgula oyster fossils. This same soil type is the primary soil in Chablis (Burgundy), which is why Chablis and Sancerre — despite using different varieties (Chardonnay vs Sauvignon Blanc) — share similar mineral depth and aging potential.
slides.6.title: Pouilly-Fumé: The Synonym for Flint Smokiness
slides.6.highlights.0.title: Silex-Dominant
slides.6.highlights.0.content: ~60% of Pouilly-Fumé is flint soil, far higher than Sancerre's 20%
slides.6.highlights.1.title: The 'Fumé' Origin Story
slides.6.highlights.1.content: French fumé means 'smoked' — named for the misty appearance of ripe grape skins reflecting sunlight, also echoing the wine's smoky aromas
slides.6.highlights.2.title: White Wine Only
slides.6.highlights.2.content: Unlike Sancerre, Pouilly-Fumé produces only Sauvignon Blanc whites (reds and rosés require Coteaux-du-Giennois)
slides.6.content:
Pouilly-Fumé faces Sancerre across the Loire River, just 5 km apart, yet produces an entirely different Sauvignon Blanc style due to differences in soil composition. Pouilly-Fumé emphasizes the ultimate expression of a single style — flint-dominant, deeply smoky — rather than Sancerre's multi-spectrum diversity.

🔥 The Double Meaning of "Fumé" (Smoky)

  1. Visual: When local grapes ripen, the gray-blue bloom (Pruina) on the grape skin reflects sunlight like mist, which farmers called blanc fumé (smoky white)
  2. Olfactory: Wines from flint soils carry a distinctive "pierre à fusil" (flint/gunpowder) aroma — a chemical characteristic of flint stone when heated

🍇 Style Characteristics

  • Aromas: Flint, smoke, gunpowder, white pepper, lime, grapefruit (more "grey-white" than Sancerre, less green citrus)
  • Palate: Firm structure, concentrated acidity, medium body; mineral sensation threads throughout
  • Aging: Top Pouilly-Fumé (e.g., Dagueneau Pur Sang, Silex) can age 15+ years, developing beeswax, nuts, smoky toast complexity

🌟 Key Producers

  • Didier Dagueneau (legacy, continued by son Louis-Benjamin): Revolutionary of Pouilly-Fumé; Pur Sang, Silex, Buisson Renard, Astéroïde series considered the world's finest Sauvignon Blanc
  • Domaine Henri Bourgeois: Family owning both Sancerre and Pouilly-Fumé; complete product range
  • Jonathan Pabiot: New generation, natural wine style
  • Château de Tracy: Long history, traditional and rigorous family estate
slides.6.quiz.question: Why is Pouilly-Fumé called "Fumé" (Smoky)? Which of the following is NOT correct?
slides.6.quiz.options.0: When grapes ripen, the gray-blue bloom on the grape skins reflects sunlight like mist
slides.6.quiz.options.1: The wine carries the pierre à fusil gunpowder aroma from heated flint soil
slides.6.quiz.options.2: The local tradition uses smoked barrels for aging
slides.6.quiz.options.3: Distinguishes varietal character from Pouilly-sur-Loire (which uses Chasselas)
slides.6.quiz.explanation: Pouilly-Fumé does not use smoked barrels — most top-tier wines even use stainless steel tanks to preserve pure mineral character. The "Fumé" name comes from the visual effect of reflected grape skins and the smoky aromas from flint soil — a natural product of geology and variety interaction, not a winemaking technique.
slides.7.title: Centre-Loire's Satellite AOCs
slides.7.highlights.0.title: Value Benchmarks
slides.7.highlights.0.content: Menetou-Salon, Quincy, Reuilly typically cost half of Sancerre, with quality that holds its own
slides.7.highlights.1.title: Varietal Diversity
slides.7.highlights.1.content: Beyond Sauvignon Blanc, some AOCs also produce Pinot Gris, Pinot Noir reds and rosés
slides.7.content:
If Sancerre and Pouilly-Fumé are the binary stars of Centre-Loire, then Menetou-Salon, Quincy, and Reuilly are nebulae worth exploring — they offer similar terroir logic at more accessible prices, excellent daily-drinking choices.

🍃 Menetou-Salon

Location: ~30 km southwest of Sancerre

Soils: Primarily Kimmeridgian marl (same origin as Sancerre Terres Blanches)

Varieties: Sauvignon Blanc (white), Pinot Noir (red/rosé)

Style: Similar to Sancerre Terres Blanches; strong mineral, priced at 60–70% of Sancerre

Notable producers: Henry Pellé, Domaine de l'Ermitage

🌾 Quincy

Location: Cher valley, west of Bourges

Soils: River terrace gravel and sand (completely different from Sancerre)

Varieties: Sauvignon Blanc white wine only

Style: Expressive fruit, lively acidity, softer palate; highly approachable

Notable producers: Domaine Trotereau, Mardon

🌸 Reuilly

Location: West of Quincy, Indre valley

Soils: Gravel, clay-limestone, schist mix

Varieties: Sauvignon Blanc (white), Pinot Noir, Pinot Gris (red/rosé)

Style: Diverse styles; Pinot Gris rosé especially distinctive (rare)

Notable producers: Claude Lafond, Denis Jamain

🌄 Coteaux-du-Giennois

Location: North of Pouilly-Fumé

Soils: Flint, chalky limestone, clay

Varieties: Sauvignon Blanc (white), Pinot Noir + Gamay (red/rosé)

Style: Light reds paired with fresh whites; village-level wine style
slides.9.title: Level 3-9 Knowledge Test
slides.9.questions.0.question: The primary stylistic difference between Sancerre and Pouilly-Fumé comes from?
slides.9.questions.0.options.1: Different soil composition ratios (Sancerre has three coexisting soils; Pouilly-Fumé is flint-dominant)
slides.9.questions.0.explanation: Both share the same climate (separated by the Loire River, only 5 km apart) and the same variety (both Sauvignon Blanc-dominant). The key difference lies in the soil: Pouilly-Fumé has ~60% flint, producing a strong smoky pierre à fusil style; Sancerre has three coexisting soils (Caillottes 40% / Terres Blanches 40% / Silex 20%), producing a more diverse style spectrum.
slides.9.questions.1.question: What is the biggest difference between Pouilly-sur-Loire and Pouilly-Fumé?
slides.9.questions.1.options.0: Grape variety — Pouilly-sur-Loire uses Chasselas; Pouilly-Fumé uses Sauvignon Blanc
slides.9.questions.1.explanation: Pouilly-sur-Loire is from the same administrative area but uses Chasselas grapes to produce light white wine; far less notable than Pouilly-Fumé. When AOC classification was established in 1937, both were listed: those using Sauvignon Blanc are labeled "Pouilly-Fumé" (also called Blanc Fumé de Pouilly), while those using Chasselas are labeled "Pouilly-sur-Loire."
slides.9.questions.2.question: Didier Dagueneau brought a revolutionary influence to which AOC?
slides.9.questions.2.explanation: Didier Dagueneau (1956–2008) was a revolutionary for Pouilly-Fumé. He introduced the concept of single-vineyard wines, reduced yields, and strictly controlled ripeness, producing the Pur Sang, Silex, Buisson Renard, and Astéroïde series that elevated Pouilly-Fumé from "affordable Sancerre alternative" to the world's finest Sauvignon Blanc. His son Louis-Benjamin Dagueneau continues to maintain this high standard.
slides.9.questions.3.question: Among Centre-Loire's satellite AOCs, which is known for its rare Pinot Gris rosé?
slides.9.questions.3.explanation: Reuilly is one of the very few AOCs in Centre-Loire that officially allows using Pinot Gris to produce rosé (vin gris style). These rosés have a delicate color nearly copper in hue, with rose petal and red fruit aromas — a very distinctive offering in France.
